senses.gloss:
ITA-1.5.3 śākhā शाखा
Branch of knowledge
Ayurveda is considered a branch of knowledge because it is derived from other Indian knowledge systems such as the Vedas.

ITA-3.1.23 śākhā शाखा
Upper and lower limbs
Five prominences in the developing fetus which correspond to the four limbs and head.

ITA-4.8.21 śākhāgatiḥ शाखागतिः
Shifting of dosha from gut to structual components
Physiological or pathological movements of dosha towards the structural components; diseases become manifest when the vitiated dosha gets dislodged in structural components .

ITA-3.16.5 Śākhāmarma शाखामर्म
Vulnerable location(s) in the limbs
Marma located in the limbs.

ITA-1.5.1 śāstram, sūtram, śākhāvidyā, jñānam, tantram, vidhiḥ, vijñānam, lakṣaṇam शास्त्रम्, सूत्रम्, शाखाविद्या, ज्ञानम्, तन्त्रम्, विधिः, विज्ञानम्, लक्षणम्
Knowledge system or treatise
A knowledge system is concise and informative and offers both theoretical and practical knowledge in its many subdisciplines. Ayurveda is considered as a knowledge system.

ITA-5.15.3 śākhāśritakāmalā शाखाश्रितकामला
Jaundice affecting body tissues such as blood and limbs
A disorder characterized by some or all the following signs and symptoms: yellow-coloured eyes; yellowish discoloration of urine; yellow-coloured skin; whitish stools; gurgling intestinal sounds/borborygmi; constipation/abdominal fullness; heaviness of heart region; pitta entering into tvaca and dhātu with gradual development of weakness; gradual development of pain in sides of chest; gradual development of hiccups; gradual development of breathlessness; gradual development of loss of taste; gradual development of fever.
